_meta.indication: Treatment of Friedreich's ataxia in adults and adolescents aged 16 years and older

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 1402 Part 2 (Study 408-C-1402; MOXIe), i.e. Study 1 in the label
pivotal_trials.phase: Pivotal Phase 2 study (Part 2 of the two-part Study 1402)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 16 to 40 years of age with genetically confirmed Friedreich's ataxia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in the modified Friedreich's Ataxia Rating Scale (mFARS) score at Week 48 in the Full Analysis Population of patients without pes cavus
pivotal_trials.n: 103 patients randomized 1:1 (SKYCLARYS n=51, placebo n=52); primary Full Analysis Population n=82
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant treatment difference (SKYCLARYS minus placebo) in mFARS change from baseline at Week 48 of -2.41 points (95% CI -4.32, -0.51; p=0.0138)

key_safety: Generally well tolerated with no deaths in the controlled study. Most common adverse reactions (>=20% and greater than placebo): elevated liver enzymes AST/ALT (37% vs 2%), headache (37% vs 25%), nausea (33% vs 13%), abdominal pain (29% vs 6%), fatigue (24% vs 14%), diarrhea (20% vs 10%), musculoskeletal pain (20% vs 15%). Warnings: elevation of aminotransferases, elevation of BNP, and lipid abnormalities.
target_moa: Omaveloxolone is postulated to activate the transcription factor Nrf2 (nuclear factor erythroid 2-like 2), which regulates the cellular response to oxidative stress and restores mitochondrial function, thereby restoring redox balance and reducing inflammation in FA, where Nrf2 signaling is impaired due to frataxin deficiency.
modality: Small molecule (semi-synthetic oleanane triterpenoid), oral capsule

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected in the intended population

summary.text: Skyclarys (omaveloxolone) received traditional approval via a Priority review NDA for Friedreich's ataxia, supported by a single adequate and well-controlled study (Study 1402 Part 2) plus confirmatory evidence. It had orphan drug designation for FA (granted June 19, 2017), and the sponsor received a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. The application was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: The Applicant has submitted data intended to support the approval of omaveloxolone for the treatment of FA based on a single, adequate, and well-controlled investigation and confirmatory evidence.
